extensions.self_hash_recipe: artifacts[0] is SELF-REFERENTIAL: a file cannot contain its own sha256. The value stored there is therefore a well-defined, third-party-reproducible quantity rather than a naive whole-file digest. RECIPE: read this file as bytes, replace the 64 hex characters of artifacts[0].sha256 with 64 ASCII zeros, sha256 the result. That must equal the stored value. Substituting 64 hex for 64 zeros is length-preserving, so artifacts[0].bytes is the TRUE on-disk size and can be checked directly with stat. Disclosed here because a reducer that re-hashes the whole file naively will see a mismatch and must apply this recipe instead of reporting a defect.

self_critique.strongest_attack_on_this_receipt: The OpenAI models page and the OpenAI pricing page disagree about gpt-5.3-codex. This receipt resolved that in favour of the pricing page (id ACTIVE, price $1.75/$14.00). Had it trusted the models page alone, it would have called an actively-priced model retired -- a false positive of exactly the kind this unit exists to catch. NC4 records that near-miss rather than hiding it.
self_critique.second_attack: Every vendor reading in this receipt was obtained through WebFetch, whose page-to-answer step is itself a model. The mitigation is that each load-bearing retirement was read off TWO different pages (and for OpenAI, additionally off a search index), and the runtime probes -- which are pure process execution -- are independent of that channel entirely.
self_critique.what_would_change_the_verdict: A vendor-published statement that claude-opus-4-1 / claude-sonnet-4-0 / claude-3-5-haiku-latest still resolve as aliases to a live snapshot would downgrade CAP-1..4 from REFUTED to PARTIAL. The deprecations page's own definition ('Requests to retired models will fail') and the dated retirement rows make that unlikely.
